selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main point is made about why life was created within the universe?
questions.answer: Life is presented as a summary of the whole universe in which many Divine purposes and Names are gathered together.

questions.question: What does the passage say was focused within life?
questions.answer: Manifestations of Divine Names and Divine purposes were focused within it.

questions.question: According to the passage, how is seeking provision connected to one of the purposes of the universe?
questions.answer: The act of receiving and pursuing provision leads creatures to thank and worship their Lord, which is one of the meaningful wisdoms in creation.

questions.question: How is the response of creatures to this blessing described?
questions.answer: It is described as constant, widespread, and rooted in gratitude.

questions.question: What pushes human beings and animals to go after their sustenance?
questions.answer: Need for food and the pleasure connected with it drive them to seek it.

questions.question: What two motivations are said to propel creatures toward provision?
questions.answer: Their need and the pleasure associated with sustenance propel them.

questions.question: What would a person with a complete view of the earth be able to notice?
questions.answer: Such a person would see the beauty of Divine mercy and providing power shown in how creatures are fed.

questions.question: How is the tree used to support that point?
questions.answer: The tree is an example of a being whose nourishment comes to it without active pursuit.

questions.question: Through what means does this provision reach animals?
questions.answer: It comes through plants, trees, and mothers.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the arrival of springtime provision after winter scarcity?
questions.answer: It portrays it as merciful aid arriving just when animals most need it.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the relationship between the cosmos and life?
questions.answer: Life is shown as a condensed reflection of the cosmos, carrying within it many of the meanings found in the whole creation.

questions.question: How is provision treated inside the domain of life?
questions.answer: It is treated as a main focal point that shapes the activity of living beings.

questions.question: Why is the sense of appetite important in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: It explains how creatures are led to recognize blessings and answer them with thankfulness and worship.

questions.question: What larger scene is described to explain Divine lordship?
questions.answer: A scene is described in which all realms of existence are enlivened and gladdened in fitting ways.

questions.question: What examples are given of realms being gladdened?
questions.answer: The heavens are gladdened by angelic beings, the unseen realm by spirits, and the earthly world by living creatures.

questions.question: How are need and pleasure connected in the search for sustenance?
questions.answer: Need pushes creatures to seek food, and pleasure makes that search active and ongoing.

questions.question: What practical result comes from this design?
questions.answer: It keeps them active instead of idle.

questions.question: What special vision is imagined in the final paragraph of the passage?
questions.answer: A vision that can take in the entire earth at one moment is imagined.

questions.question: What would an all-seeing observer discover at the end of winter?
questions.answer: That animals are met with fresh, abundant nourishment at the very time they need it most.

questions.question: What central lesson about mercy and provision ties the whole passage together?
questions.answer: The whole passage teaches that sustenance across creation is arranged by one wise and compassionate Provider.

questions.question: What is the first major claim in the passage about the creation of life?
questions.answer: Life was created as a comprehensive expression of the universe.

questions.question: Why were living things given enjoyment in provision?
questions.answer: So their search for sustenance would become a path to thankfulness and worship.

questions.question: What would happen to animal sustenance if the wisdom behind striving did not exist?
questions.answer: Their food would come straight to them without effort.

questions.question: How is the new supply of food for animals described?
questions.answer: It is portrayed as rich, pleasant, varied, and timely help sent from Divine mercy.
